about.title: Fremont Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fremont sits at a crossroads of the East Bay, and its roads carry the traffic to prove it. In 2025, public records show 799 injury collisions across the city, leaving 1,069 people hurt and 14 killed. Many of those crashes clustered along I-880, both directions of I-680, and Fremont Boulevard, with a noticeable bump on Friday evenings between 5 and 7 p.m. as commuters head home across Alameda County. If one of those collisions involved you, the days that follow can feel disorienting. Medical bills arrive before the insurance adjuster returns your call. Meanwhile, California gives you two years to file a claim, and only six months in many cases involving a public agency, such as a city vehicle or a poorly maintained roadway. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that matches Fremont residents with an independent personal injury attorney who handles car accident cases on contingency. You pay nothing to be connected, and the attorney collects a fee only if your case results in a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Fremont Drivers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: You Keep the Clock in View
items.desc: California's two-year filing window shrinks to as little as six months when a government entity is involved. The attorney you're matched with can sort out which deadline applies before it slips by.

items.title: Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover even if you were partly responsible; your share of fault simply reduces the amount. An attorney can push back when an insurer tries to inflate your percentage.

items.title: No Fee Unless There's a Recovery
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so you owe nothing upfront and nothing at all if your case doesn't result in a recovery. Our matching service is free as well.

items.question: I was hit on I-680 near the Fremont exits. Does it matter that it happened on a freeway rather than a city street?
items.answer: The location can affect which police agency wrote the report and who may share responsibility, but your right to pursue a claim is the same. Freeway crashes often involve multiple vehicles or higher speeds, which can make fault more contested. Gathering the CHP report, photos, and witness contacts early gives your attorney more to work with.

items.question: The other driver's insurance company wants a recorded statement. Should I give one?
items.answer: You are not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's generally wise to decline until you've spoken with an attorney. Adjusters may use small inconsistencies to argue you were more at fault or less injured than you are. A short, factual report to your own insurer is a different matter and usually required by your policy.

items.question: What should I save after a Fremont car accident?
items.answer: Keep every photo of the vehicles, the roadway, and your injuries, along with repair estimates, medical records, and any dashcam footage. Write down the names of witnesses and note the time and weather, since conditions on corridors like Fremont Boulevard can change quickly. Hold onto damaged personal items and don't authorize your car's repair or disposal until the evidence has been documented.
